title: Subcontractor Document Tracker
summary: Insurance and certificates of subcontractors expire unnoticed, which is a legal risk. AI reads the documents and chases renewals.
hook: "The roofer's insurance expired two months ago. Nobody noticed. Then he fell."
story:
**A facility-services company manages cleaning, maintenance and repairs** using 40 subcontractors. Each subcontractor must have valid **liability insurance, a business registration, safety certificates and sometimes permits**, and the big clients (property owners, industrial sites) demand proof.

Today it's an Excel sheet and a folder of PDFs. Documents expire silently. When a client audit comes, someone spends **days chasing** subcontractors. If an accident happens while insurance has lapsed, the main company is liable.

whyReal.title: Legal and financial risk
whyReal.text: Working with uninsured or unregistered subcontractors can make the main contractor liable. That fear sells.

whyReal.title: Big clients demand it
whyReal.text: Property owners and industrial sites require proof of compliance from everyone on site.

whyReal.title: Constant chasing
whyReal.text: Documents expire at different dates; chasing 40 subcontractors by email never ends.

whyReal.title: Jonatan sells to this industry
whyReal.text: His window-cleaning company works on commercial and industrial sites. He knows the buyers.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: general contractors, facility-management and cleaning companies, property managers with 10+ subcontractors.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: owner, operations manager or HSE (health & safety) manager.

whoPays.label: Market
whoPays.text: start in Sweden/Nordics through Jonatan, but the problem is global (in the US, insurance-certificate tracking is a known category).

solution.title: Invite
solution.text: add subcontractors; each gets a link (no login needed).

solution.title: Upload
solution.text: they upload insurance, registration and certificates as photos or PDFs.

solution.title: Read
solution.text: AI reads each document and extracts type, company name, coverage amounts and **expiry date**, and checks them against requirements.

solution.title: Dashboard
solution.text: green / yellow (expiring in 30 days) / red (expired or missing) for every subcontractor.

solution.title: Chase automatically
solution.text: reminders at 30, 14 and 3 days before expiry until a new document arrives.

solution.title: Audit-ready
solution.text: one click exports a full compliance pack for a client.

later: Integration with business registries (check company status)

timeline.what: **Validate.** Jonatan calls 20 facility/construction companies. For 2 of them, we collect their subcontractor docs and build the tracker manually in a spreadsheet.
Reminders, export pack, first paid customers.

risks.answer: Start with Sweden; make requirements configurable.
No-login link, SMS reminders, and the main company makes it mandatory.
Human confirm on first upload; highlight low confidence.
Expand from facility services to construction and property management.

questions: How many subcontractors do you work with? What documents do you require from them?
How do you track expiry dates today?
Have you ever discovered a subcontractor's insurance had expired? What happened?
Do your clients audit your subcontractors? How long does preparing take?
What would it be worth to never chase a document again?
